title: Anagram Pairs

statement.markdown:
Given an array of lowercase words, count how many pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j` are **anagrams** of each other — same letters, same multiplicities, any order.

Comparing every pair is O(n²·L). Can you group words so all anagrams land in the same bucket?

examples.explanation: All three are mutual anagrams: 3 pairs.

hints: Two words are anagrams exactly when some canonical form of them is identical. What canonical form?
Sort each word's letters — anagrams collapse to the same key. Count bucket sizes in a hash map.
A bucket of c mutual anagrams contributes c·(c−1)/2 pairs. Sum over buckets.
solutionExplanation: Canonicalize each word by sorting its letters; anagrams share the key. Count each key's bucket size c, and each bucket contributes C(c,2) = c(c−1)/2 pairs. Time O(n · L log L), space O(n·L) — versus O(n²) pairwise comparison.
